faqs.q: What is the best time to visit offbeat places in Rajasthan?
faqs.a: October to March is the best time for most of Rajasthan, when days are pleasant and dry and migratory birds arrive at wetlands such as Menar. Summers are very hot, especially in desert areas like Barmer, though greener regions such as Jhalawar also look lovely during the monsoon.

faqs.q: Which hidden gems in Rajasthan can be visited from Udaipur?
faqs.a: From Udaipur you can reach several lesser-known places by road, including the bird village of Menar, the hill fort of Kumbhalgarh, the marble Jain temple at Ranakpur and the lake town of Dungarpur. Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur are often combined in one trip because they lie on the same side of Udaipur.

faqs.q: Is Kumbhalgarh Fort a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.a: Yes. Kumbhalgarh Fort is one of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan listed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha in the Aravalli Hills, it is known for its very long fortified wall, temples and views over the surrounding hills.

faqs.q: What is the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan famous for?
faqs.a: Shekhawati in northern Rajasthan is famous for its painted havelis, built by wealthy merchants in the 18th and 19th centuries and covered in colourful frescoes of myths, folk tales and scenes from the British era. Towns such as Mandawa and Nawalgarh are so full of murals that the region is called an open-air art gallery.
